'''{{ill|Mifune Shrine|ja|御船神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mifune Shrine|qq=}}''' (*Mifune Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (the Inner Shrine of the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}), located in {{ill|Taki, Mie|en|Taki, Mie|qid=Q1203963|lt=Taki Town|1=Taki, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. This article also covers the co-located '''{{ill|Mifune Shrine|lt=Mifune Shrine|lt=Mumino Shrine|ja|牟弥乃神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mumino Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御船神社 (多気町)}}''' (*Mumino Jinja*), a subordinate shrine (*massha*).

Both shrines enshrine deities associated with rivers and water (*{{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god|1=Suijin}}*).<ref name="ic">Ise Culture Publishing (2008): p. 64.</ref>

== Overview ==
This section describes the common aspects of the two shrines.

{{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}{{ill|Taki District, Mie|en|Taki District, Mie|qid=Q1042360|lt=Taki District|1=Taki District, Mie}}{{ill|Taki, Mie|en|Taki, Mie|qid=Q1203963|lt=Taki Town|1=Taki, Mie}} '''Toba''' (土羽) is enshrined at the location.<ref name="sk8">式内社研究会 編（1990）：378ページ</ref> The place name {{ill|place name|ja|地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/place name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Toponym|qid=Q7884789}} “Toba” (土羽) means “stopping place”, and it is derived from the boat of {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Wahime no Mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} having stopped there.<ref name="tc5">金子（1983）：55ページ</ref>

The shrine building {{ill|Shrine building|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|1=Shinto architecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}} is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} style and is surrounded by a {{ill|Tamagaki|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Gyokugaki|1=Sacred fences}}. There is no {{ill|Saisen|en|Saisen|qid=Q988479|lt=offertory box|1=Saisen}}. An {{ill|Nightlight|en|Nightlight|qid=Q762277|lt=eternal lantern|1=Nightlight}} stands at the entrance of the shrine grounds.<ref name="ic"/> The area of the shrine grounds is 975 {{ill|Pyeong|en|Pyeong|qid=Q706688|lt=tsubo|1=Pyeong}} (≈3,223 {{ill|Square metre|en|Square metre|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>|1=Square metre}}).<ref name="sk0">式内社研究会 編（1990）：380ページ</ref>

== Mifune Shrine (御船神社) ==
Mifune Shrine (御船神社) is the 24th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：9 - 11ページ</ref> It is the shrine established when {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Wahime no Mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, while journeying upstream on the Tokidagawa (外城田川, Tokidagawa), anchored her boat and designated the site.<ref name="ic"/> She stopped here because the river narrowed and her boat could no longer pass.<ref name="tc5"/>

In the ''Engishiki Shinnamyochō'', it is recorded as “Ōkami no Mifune Shrine” (大神乃御船神社).<ref name="sk8"/> The term “Ōkami no Mifune” is understood to mean the boat on which {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|1=Amaterasu}} rides, and Sonoda Moriyoshi conjectured that the boat-keeper’s office, which enshrined the sacred object of Amaterasu, was transferred to Mifune Shrine after her relocation.<ref name="sk8"/>

The deity enshrined is Ōmikagegawa-no-Kami (大神御蔭川神).<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">学研パブリッシング（2013）：68ページ</ref> It is regarded as either the guardian deity ({{ill|Guardian deities|lt=Guardian deities|lt=Guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guardian deity|qq=}}) of the Tokidagawa, which irrigates the fields, or as the protector of water transportation.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> The same deity is also enshrined at {{ill|Kano Shrine|ja|狭田国生神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kano Shrine|qq=}}, another auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine, as a {{ill|Deity|en|Deity|qid=Q178885|lt=Deity|1=Deity}}.<ref>金子（1983）：59ページ</ref> The term “Mikage” denotes a spirit or beneficence, and the ''Jingū Tenryaku'' explains that it is the spirit of the great deity enshrined by the river that diverts water to {{ill|Kanda|ja|神田|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanda|1=Shinden (divine field)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10855080}}.<ref name="sk9">式内社研究会 編（1990）：379ページ</ref>

There are alternative theories regarding the deity; the ''Ise Nisho Taijingū Shinmyōhisho'' calls it “Ōkami no Mifune Shin”, the ''Engishiki Shinmyōchō Hetsuan-shū'' refers to it as “Tenchōsen Shin”, and the ''Ise-koku Shinmyōchō Kōshō'' names it “Toriishi Kusen Shin”.<ref name="sk0"/>

== Mumino Shrine (牟弥乃神社) ==
Mumino Shrine (牟弥乃神社) is the 15th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：13 - 14ページ</ref> Its shrine building is no longer extant and it is co-located with Mifune Shrine.<ref>宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：14ページ</ref>

The deities enshrined are Samukawa-hiko-no-Mikoto (寒川比古命) and Samukawa-hime-no-Mikoto (寒川比女命).<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> They are regarded as the guardian deities of the Tokidagawa and are the children of Ōminakami-no-Mikoto (大水上命).<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> The name “Samukawa” is an alternate name for the Tokidagawa, derived from the fact that its water was cold, which led {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Wahime no Mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} to name it so.<ref name="tc5"/>

== History ==
According to the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, Mifune Shrine was established by the time the ''Engishiki Shinnamyochō'' was compiled, that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|en|Enchō|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|927|en|927|qid=Q30470|lt=927|1=927}}).<ref name="ic2">伊勢文化舎（2008）：22ページ</ref> The ''Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō'' records it as “Wahime Naishinnō Teishuku” (倭姫内親王定祝).<ref name="sk8"/> Since it is mentioned in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō'', it is inferred that the shrine existed prior to the 23rd year of {{ill|Enryaku|en|Enryaku|qid=Q1373176|lt=Enryaku|1=Enryaku}} ({{ill|804|en|804|qid=Q29998|lt=804|1=804}}).<ref name="ic2"/>

In ancient times, Toba belonged to the Tanabe area of [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Togai District]] (田辺郷). However, in the 5th year of {{ill|Taika (era)|en|Taika (era)|qid=Q1077930|lt=Taika|1=Taika (era)}} ({{ill|649|en|649|qid=Q31117|lt=649|1=649}}), {{ill|Taki District, Mie|en|Taki District, Mie|qid=Q1042360|lt=Taki District|1=Taki District, Mie}} was separated from Togai District, and Toba came to belong to the Yūri area (有尓郷) of the new district.<ref name="tc5"/> Accordingly, in the ''Engishiki Shinnamyochō'', it is listed under Togai District as “Ōkami no Mifune Shrine”.<ref name="sk9"/>

From the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|qid=Q12554|lt=Medieval|1=Middle Ages}} period onwards, the rites were discontinued, and the shrine was revived at its present location in the 3rd year of {{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|qid=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun|1=Kanbun (era)}} ({{ill|August 29 (Lunisolar)|ja|8月29日 (旧暦)}} {{ill|Gregorian calendar|en|Gregorian calendar|qid=Q12138|lt=Gregorian calendar|1=Gregorian calendar}}: {{ill|1663|en|1663|qid=Q7577|lt=1663|1=1663}}, {{ill|September 30|en|September 30|qid=Q2881|lt=September 30|1=September 30}}).<ref name="sk8"/> At that time, traces of a moat ({{ill|Moat|en|Moat|qid=Q88480|lt=Moat|1=Moat}}), old pillar holes, and decayed wood were discovered, suggesting the site of the original shrine.<ref>式内社研究会 編（1990）：378 - 379ページ</ref> While {{ill|Mikoto Kiyonao|ja|御巫清直|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikoto Kiyonao|1=Mikannagi Kiyonao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6537624}} supported the theory that this location was the original shrine site, Nakagawa Tsuneaki argued that the village deity ({{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|qid=Q767655|lt=Ujigami|1=Ujigami}}), colloquially known as “Mifune-sha”, of a neighboring village in Toba Village, was the original shrine.<ref name="sk9"/> In the 14th year of {{ill|Tenpō|en|Tenpō|qid=Q1369045|lt=Tenpō|1=Tenpō}} ({{ill|1843|en|1843|qid=Q7629|lt=1843|1=1843}}), an eternal lantern was installed at the shrine entrance.<ref name="gk"/>

In {{ill|Meiji 4|ja|明治4|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji 4|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{ill|1871|en|1871|qid=Q7746|lt=1871|1=1871}}), Mumino Shrine, whose original location had been unknown since the Medieval period, was relocated to be co-located with Mifune Shrine.<ref name="sk0"/>

== Transportation ==
; Public Transportation
* From {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR|1=Central Japan Railway Company}} {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangu Line|1=Sangū Line}} {{ill|Tokida Station|en|Tokida Station|qid=Q7813584|lt=Tokido Station|1=Tokida Station}}, it is about a 17-minute walk (approximately 900m).<ref name="ic-P63">伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：63ページ</ref> From the station's main (southern) exit, walk along {{ill|Miyakawa Waterway|ja|宮川用水|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakawa Waterway|1=Q11454721|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11454721}}, and the elevated area visible on the right is where Mifune Shrine and Mumino Shrine are located.<ref name="ic"/>
; By Private Car
* From {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway|1=Ise Expressway}} {{ill|Tamashiro Interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|lt=Tamashiro IC|lt_ja=玉城IC|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamashiro Interchange|1=Tamaki interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11572465}}, it is about a 14-minute drive (approximately 5.9 {{ill|Kilometre|en|Kilometre|qid=Q828224|lt=km|1=Kilometre}}). There is no {{ill|Parking lot|en|Parking lot|qid=Q6501349|lt=parking lot|1=Parking lot}} nearby.
